newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia expects grain crop to fall short of target.
newsitem.headline: Georgia expects grain crop to fall short of target.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Georgia expects a 1996 grain crop of 500,000 tonnes for 1996, down from 531,000 tonnes in 1995 and significantly less than hoped for earlier, the agriculture ministry said on Friday.

A ministry spokesman said 145,000 tonnes of wheat had already been threshed out of a forecast of 163,000 tonnes. Most of the expected wheat crop, 124,000 tonnes, will be milling wheat. Last years wheat harvest was 125,000 tonnes.
The ministry said lack of cash for fertilizers and proper harvesting led to a lacklustre harvest. The government had planned at the beginning of the year to reap 360,000 tonnes of wheat.
The fall in production comes despite a significant increase in area sown to grain, at 420,000 hectares after 280,000 in 1995.
Maize production is expected to total 300,000 tonnes on 225,000 hectares, down from 350,000 tonnes last year.
Maize plantings were up significantly after 125,000 hectares in 1995.
The ministry had planned at the beginning of the year to on produce 600,000 tonnes of grain. The southern republic consumes about 600,000 tonnes of feed grains and 200,000 of milling wheat each year.
This year it has imported 300,000 tonnes of grain, 80,000 of which was in the form of humanitarian aid, the ministry spokesman added.
